repository_verification.verified_files_sha256_note: Digests as reviewed at repository.commit. Frozen evidence: do not rewrite them to make a suite green. A file that has knowingly moved since review belongs in accepted_drift_sha256 with a reason.

Written/ViewModels/DistillViewModel.swif.reason: Disconnect all names both schemas, and the raw archive is wired to the same lifecycle points. The first half is unchanged and stands: it deleted every local record including source='user', so a person who asked for their music and calendar to go came back to a profile with no school and no occupation; it now keeps what somebody typed, which is the same line SyncService.deleteEverything draws server-side. It then calls SemanticSurfaceService.forgetDistillation, the vault half that never existed — deleteEverything empties four tables in public and names none of the ones Memories reads, so every term stayed on that page after the sources behind it were gone. A failure there is reported separately and does not stop the local clearing, because the sources really are disconnected. distillationCleared is bumped so Memories reloads without waiting for a visit that never comes, Settings being raised from that screen. runningSources drives the per-source distilling animation, which fired once for a batch and so looked absent on consecutive sources; signOutLocalState clears ProfilePhotoCache beside ChatStore, other people's faces being held under an authorisation that ends with the session. The second half (45fdeca) adds RawArchive at four seams. flush() rides the dual-write's detached task and shares nothing with it — not the summary, not saveError, not the coverage report — because a shadow path that can break the live one is not a shadow; the files are on disk before it runs, so a refused upload costs a retry rather than the data. forget() runs on sign-out, detached, since a sign-out must not wait on a directory walk. Disconnect all calls forget() and forget_raw_archives(): the third deletion place and the easiest to forget, and erasing the readings while keeping the bodies they were derived from is the worse of the two arrangements — precisely what 'a deletion control names both schemas or it is not finished' was written about. And 'Download my data' now hands over a bundle rather than the eight columns of Written's reading; the CSV is unchanged and travels inside it under its old name, so a spreadsheet built on the old file still opens. THIS DOES CHANGE WHAT LEAVES THE DEVICE — gzipped raw bodies to a private raw-source-archives bucket only their owner may read — and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy, web/en-us/privacy/index.html and CLAUDE.md moved in the same commit, which is the rule. HealthKit and Location are excluded from the archive: for both, discarding is the declaration PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy makes, and an archive would have quietly made it false.

Written/Services/Ontology.swift.reason: A calendar term now reports its provider rather than its connector. `event.source` reads `apple_calendar` for an Outlook or Google account added in iOS Settings, because EventKit is how those arrive, so a term from an Outlook dinner claimed it came from Apple Calendar. It carries `event.provider`, read from the `cal_type` and `account` the distiller stamps; rows collected before that stamping read `other` rather than being guessed at.

Written/Services/SyncService.swift.reason: `deleteSource` names both schemas, and `isLocalOnly` can now be asked before a record exists. The first half is unchanged and stands: it deleted from `public.distilled_records` and `public.source_connections` and stopped there, so a disconnected source kept every observation and every encrypted record in the vault — measured 2026-08-15 on a real account that had disconnected Spotify: 580 active observations and 593 raw records still resolved, still scored, still read by the catalogue mint. It calls `api.forget_source` (0185) after the public half and returns the failure rather than swallowing it. The vault's own source code goes over the wire, asked of `SemanticSource.forAppSource` rather than reproduced, because `healthkit` and `health` are one of the two translation seams. The semantic side needs no change: the RPC is the semantic side. The second half (45fdeca) is `isLocalOnlyType(source:dataType:)`, which `isLocalOnly(_:)` now delegates to. RawArchive captures at the framework query, before anything has become a DistilledRecord, so the refusal has to be askable earlier — applying it after serialising would put health/biological_sex in a file on disk that the Settings export then ships. One list, asked from both ends; a second copy of that pair somewhere else is exactly how the rule stops being true without anybody deciding to break it. localOnlySources and localOnlyTypes are UNCHANGED, so this widens what may ask the question and nothing about the answer.

Written/Models/DistilledRecord.swift.reason: SourceStatus gains `.partial(count:missing:)`. `.done` could not express "worked, and did not get everything", which is how a distillation that lost five of nine data types reported a count, grew the plant and told nobody. Measured on a device: consecutive runs carried four types and then nine. DistilledRecord itself is unchanged; the enum shares the file.

reference_migrations_note: Historical record of the standalone reference chain. Those files are deliberately NOT vendored into the Written repository: their adapted forms are application_migrations 42-47, and keeping both would be two divergent copies of the same DDL.
application_migrations_reserved_note: 50-57 carry the encrypted-vault path end to end: key registry, vocabulary alignment, the ingestion identity and its wrapped-key binding, key-write ordering, the run lifecycle, the finalize guard, and the worker identity that reads the vault back. 58 (server projections) is due in phase server_owned_discovery_and_profiles and 59 (cutover) in legacy_semantic_retirement. The pair has shifted nine times; the contract forbids reusing a number, not skipping one, so read a number in WRITTEN_REPOSITORY_INTEGRATION.md as the `role` below rather than as a filename. 59 is irreversible and must not exist on disk before a minimum supported client version does.
